  kgen.param.declare D3: scalar<si64> = <sub(D2, 4)>
  %res = mo.static.reshape(%input) : !mo.tensor<[D0], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[D3], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output %[[INPUT]] : !mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32>
  mo.output<D3> %res : !mo.tensor<[D3], f32>
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @fold_nested_max
// CHECK-SAME: <[[D0:.*]], [[BS:.*]] -> [[OUT:.*]]>(
// CHECK-SAME:   %[[INPUT:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32>,
// CHECK-SAME:   %[[DUMMY:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[BS]]], f32>
// CHECK-SAME: ) -> !mo.tensor<[[[OUT]], 768], f32> {
mo.graph @fold_nested_max<D0, bs -> out>(
  %input: !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>,
  %dummy: !mo.tensor<[bs], f32> // this is used solely to help define `bs`
) -> !mo.tensor<[out, 768], f32> {

  kgen.param.declare D1: scalar<si64> = <max(bs, 1)>
  kgen.param.declare D2: scalar<si64> = <max(D1, bs)>

  // CHECK-NEXT: %[[INPUT_RS:.*]] = mo.static.reshape(%[[INPUT]]) : !mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[max([[BS]], 1), 768], f32>
  %input_rs = mo.static.reshape(%input) : !mo.tensor<[D0], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[D1, 768], f32>

  // Simplified and removed.
  %res = mo.static.broadcast_to(%input_rs) : !mo.tensor<[D1, 768], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[D2, 768], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output<max([[BS]], 1)> %[[INPUT_RS]] : !mo.tensor<[max([[BS]], 1), 768], f32>
  mo.output<D2> %res : !mo.tensor<[D2, 768], f32>
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @non_mo_tensor_input
mo.graph @non_mo_tensor_input<D0 -> D1>(
  // CHECK-SAME: <[[D0:.*]]>(%[[INPUT:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32>, %[[SHAPE:.*]]: !mosh.ape
  %input: !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>, %shape: !mosh.ape
// CHECK-SAME: ) -> (!mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32>, !mosh.ape) {
) -> (!mo.tensor<[D1], f32>, !mosh.ape) {

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output %[[INPUT]], %[[SHAPE]] : !mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32>, !mosh.ape
  mo.output<D0> %input, %shape : !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>, !mosh.ape
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @out_of_order_instructions
// CHECK-SAME:  <[[D0:.*]] -> [[OUT:.*]]>(
// CHECK-SAME:   %[[SCALAR:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[], f32>,
// CHECK-SAME:   %[[DUMMY:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32>
// CHECK-SAME: ) -> !mo.tensor<[[[OUT]]], f32> {
mo.graph @out_of_order_instructions<D0 -> out>(
  %scalar: !mo.tensor<[], f32>,
  %dummy: !mo.tensor<[D0], f32> // this is used solely to help define `D0`
) -> !mo.tensor<[out], f32> {

  kgen.param.declare D3: scalar<si64> = <div(D2, D0)>
  kgen.param.declare D2: scalar<si64> = <mul(D1, D1)>

  // CHECK-NEXT: %[[RES:.*]] = mo.static.broadcast_to(%[[SCALAR]]) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[div(add(mul([[D0]], [[D0]]), mul([[D0]], 2), 1), [[D0]])], f32>
  %res = mo.static.broadcast_to(%scalar) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[D3], f32>

  kgen.param.declare D1: scalar<si64> = <add(D0, 1)>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output<div(add(mul([[D0]], [[D0]]), mul([[D0]], 2), 1), [[D0]])> %[[RES]] : !mo.tensor<[div(add(mul([[D0]], [[D0]]), mul([[D0]], 2), 1), [[D0]])], f32>
  mo.output<D3> %res : !mo.tensor<[D3], f32>
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @nested_mul
mo.graph @nested_mul<D0>() {

  // These KGEN expressions are all folded away

  // NOTE that this gets canonicalized into `mul(D0, 2)`
  kgen.param.declare P0: scalar<si64> = <add(D0, D0)>
  kgen.param.declare P1: scalar<si64> = <mod(P0, D0)>
  kgen.param.declare P2: scalar<bool> = <identical(:scalar<si64> P1, 0)>
  kgen.param.declare P3: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"{message = "error" : !kgen.string}, P2)>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output
  mo.output
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @range_based_folding
// CHECK-SAME:  <[[D0:.*]] -> [[O3:.*]]>(
// CHECK-SAME:    %[[IN:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[], f32>
// CHECK-SAME:  ) -> !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 0, 0, [[O3]]], f32> {
mo.graph @range_based_folding<D0 -> O0, O1, O2, O3>(
  %in: !mo.tensor<[], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[O0, O1, O2, O3], f32> {

  kgen.param.declare P0: scalar<si64> = <max(D0, 0)> // D0
  kgen.param.declare P1: scalar<si64> = <max(mul_no_wrap(D0, -1), 0)> // 0
  kgen.param.declare P2: scalar<si64> = <min(D0, 0)> // 0
  kgen.param.declare P3: scalar<si64> = <min(mul_no_wrap(D0, -1), 0)> // mul_no_wrap(D0, -1)

  // CHECK-NEXT: %[[OUT:.*]] = mo.static.broadcast_to(%[[IN]])
  // CHECK-SAME: : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 0, 0, mul_no_wrap([[D0]], -1)], f32>
  %out = mo.static.broadcast_to(%in) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[P0, P1, P2, P3], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output<mul_no_wrap([[D0]], -1)> %[[OUT]] : !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 0, 0, mul_no_wrap([[D0]], -1)], f32>
  mo.output<P0, P1, P2, P3> %out : !mo.tensor<[P0, P1, P2, P3], f32>
}


// This optimization simplifies statements of the form `<max(add(A, B), B)>`
// where we know `A, B >= 0`. We know `A, B >= 0` because they appear in a shape.
// As a result `A + B >= B` and `<max(add(A, B), B)> = add(A, B)`

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @propagate_max_add_optimization
// CHECK-SAME: <
// CHECK-SAME: [[A:[a-zA-Z0-9_]*]], [[B:[a-zA-Z0-9_]*]] ->
// CHECK-SAME: [[D1:[a-zA-Z0-9_]*]], [[D2:[a-zA-Z0-9_]*]], [[D3:[a-zA-Z0-9_]*]], [[D4:[a-zA-Z0-9_]*]]
// CHECK-SAME: >
// CHECK-SAME: (
// CHECK-SAME: [[IN:%[a-zA-Z0-9_]*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[A]], [[B]]], f32>
// CHECK-SAME: ) ->
// CHECK-SAME: (!mo.tensor<[[[D1]], 1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[[[D2]], 1], f32>,
// CHECK-SAME: !mo.tensor<[[[D3]], 1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[[[D4]], 1], f32>)
mo.graph @propagate_max_add_optimization<A, B -> D1, D2, D3, D4>
  (%arg0: !mo.tensor<[A, B], f32>) ->
  (!mo.tensor<[D1, 1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[D2, 1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[D3, 1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[D4, 1], f32>)
{
  kgen.param.declare expr1: scalar<si64> = <max(add(A, B), B)>
  kgen.param.declare expr2: scalar<si64> = <max(add(A, B), A)>
  kgen.param.declare expr3: scalar<si64> = <max(A, add(A, B))>
  kgen.param.declare expr4: scalar<si64> = <max(B, add(A, B))>

  // NOTE: no A and B exist which fulfill this rebind safely, but we just have it
  // to easily test the simplification of this MAX property.
  // CHECK-NEXT: [[V0:%.*]] = mo.rebind([[IN]]) : !mo.tensor<[[[A]], [[B]]], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[add([[A]], [[B]]), 1], f32>
  // CHECK-NEXT: [[V1:%.*]] = mo.rebind([[IN]]) : !mo.tensor<[[[A]], [[B]]], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[add([[A]], [[B]]), 1], f32>
  // CHECK-NEXT: [[V2:%.*]] = mo.rebind([[IN]]) : !mo.tensor<[[[A]], [[B]]], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[add([[A]], [[B]]), 1], f32>
  // CHECK-NEXT: [[V3:%.*]] = mo.rebind([[IN]]) : !mo.tensor<[[[A]], [[B]]], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[add([[A]], [[B]]), 1], f32>
  %a = mo.rebind(%arg0): !mo.tensor<[A, B], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[expr1, 1], f32>
  %b = mo.rebind(%arg0): !mo.tensor<[A, B], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[expr2, 1], f32>
  %c = mo.rebind(%arg0): !mo.tensor<[A, B], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[expr3, 1], f32>
  %d = mo.rebind(%arg0): !mo.tensor<[A, B], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[expr4, 1], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output
  // CHECK-SAME: [[V0]], [[V1]], [[V2]], [[V3]]
  mo.output<expr1, expr2, expr3, expr4> %a, %b, %c, %d : !mo.tensor<[expr1, 1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[expr2, 1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[expr3, 1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[expr4, 1], f32>
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @update_param_declare_rhs
// CHECK-SAME:  <[[D1:.*]]>() {
mo.graph @update_param_declare_rhs<D1>() {
  // In cases like this, where we do some folding in the RHS of a
  // `kgen.param.declare`, we still want to update the RHS to the simplified
  // version in the IR (not just in the evaluator during the pass).

  // CHECK-NEXT: kgen.param.declare {{.*}}: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"{message = "test" : !kgen.string}, identical(:scalar<si64> [[D1]], 1))>
  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output
  kgen.param.declare CH: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"{message = "test" : !kgen.string}, identical(:scalar<si64> cond(identical(:scalar<si64> D1, -1), 1, D1), 1))>
  mo.output
}

// NOTE this ensures the pass can handle out-of-order ops. The test is somewhat
// contrived, but once we have general SSA->Parameter conversion (e.g., scalar
// input in llama2 that gets used in shape computation), the pass would have to
// deal with such out-of-order cases in practice.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @out_of_order_ops
// CHECK-SAME:   <() -> [[D0:.*]], [[D1:.*]], [[D2:.*]], [[D3:.*]]>(
// CHECK-SAME:   %[[INPUT:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[], f32>,
// CHECK-SAME:   %[[SHAPE1:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[2], si32>,
// CHECK-SAME:   %[[SHAPE2:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[2], si32>
// CHECK-SAME: ) -> (!mo.tensor<[[[D0]], [[D1]]], f32>, !mo.tensor<[[[D2]], [[D3]]], f32>) {
mo.graph @out_of_order_ops<() -> D0, D1, D2, D3>(
  %input: !mo.tensor<[], f32>,
  %shape1: !mo.tensor<[2], si32>,
  %shape2: !mo.tensor<[2], si32>
) -> (!mo.tensor<[D0, D1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[D2, D3], f32>) {

  // NOTE that SSA dependencies are all preserved, but not parameter
  // dependencies. Moreover, there's a transitive dependency to `%b1` as well
  // (due to the shape function call below). The pass must handle such
  // transitive dependencies across SSA/Param boundaries.
  %b2 = mo.static.broadcast_to(%input): !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[D6, D7], f32>

  mo.invoke_shape_func["mo.broadcast_to"]<() -> D4, D5>(%input, %shape1)
    [dataDeptTensors = [1]] :
    (!mo.tensor<[], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si32>)
  %b1 = mo.static.broadcast_to(%input): !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[D4, D5], f32>

  mo.invoke_shape_func["mo.broadcast_to"]<() -> D6, D7>(%b1, %shape2)
    [dataDeptTensors = [1]] :
    (!mo.tensor<[D4, D5], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si32>)

  // NOTE that these got sorted based on SSA _and_ parameter dependencies.
  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.invoke_shape_func["mo.broadcast_to"]<() -> [[D4:.*]], [[D5:.*]]>(%[[INPUT]], %[[SHAPE1]])
  // CHECK-SAME:   [dataDeptTensors = [1]] :
  // CHECK-SAME:   (!mo.tensor<[], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si32>)
  //
  // CHECK-NEXT: %[[B1:.*]] = mo.static.broadcast_to(%[[INPUT]]) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[[[D4]], [[D5]]], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.invoke_shape_func["mo.broadcast_to"]<() -> [[D6:.*]], [[D7:.*]]>(%[[B1]], %[[SHAPE2]])
  // CHECK-SAME:   [dataDeptTensors = [1]] :
  // CHECK-SAME:   (!mo.tensor<[[[D4]], [[D5]]], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si32>)
  //
  // CHECK-NEXT: %[[B2:.*]] = mo.static.broadcast_to(%[[INPUT]]) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[[[D6]], [[D7]]], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output<[[D4]], [[D5]], [[D6]], [[D7]]> %[[B1]], %[[B2]] : !mo.tensor<[[[D4]], [[D5]]], f32>, !mo.tensor<[[[D6]], [[D7]]], f32>
  mo.output<D4, D5, D6, D7> %b1, %b2 : !mo.tensor<[D4, D5], f32>, !mo.tensor<[D6, D7], f32>
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @broadcast_to_parametric_shape
// CHECK-SAME:   <[[D0:.*]], [[D1:.*]]>(
// CHECK-SAME:    %[[INPUT:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32>,
// CHECK-SAME:    %[[DUMMY:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D1]]], f32>
// CHECK-SAME:  ) -> !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], [[D1]]], f32> {
mo.graph @broadcast_to_parametric_shape<D0, D1 -> D2, D3>(
  %input: !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>,
  %dummy: !mo.tensor<[D1], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[D2, D3], f32> {

  %param_shape = mosh.param.to_value: !mosh.ape = <[D0, D1]>
  %target_shape = mo.shape.to_tensor(%param_shape) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: kgen.param.declare {{.*}}: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"
  // CHECK-SAME:  {message = "[broadcast_to] input dimension at index 0 ([[D0]]) must be either 1 or equal to corresponding output dimension at index 1 ([[D1]])" : !kgen.string},
  // CHECK-SAME:  or(identical(:scalar<si64> D0, D1), identical(:scalar<si64> D0, 1)))>
  //
  // CHECK-NEXT: %[[RES:.*]] = mo.static.broadcast_to(%[[INPUT]])
  // CHECK-SAME:   : !mo.tensor<[[[D0]]], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], [[D1]]], f32>
  %res = mo.broadcast_to<() -> D4, D5>(%input, %target_shape) : (
    !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si32>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[D4, D5], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output %[[RES]] : !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], [[D1]]], f32>
  mo.output<D4, D5> %res : !mo.tensor<[D4, D5], f32>
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @reshape_parametric_shape
// CHECK-SAME:   <[[D0:.*]], [[D1:.*]]>(
// CHECK-SAME:    %[[INPUT:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], [[D1]]], f32>
// CHECK-SAME:  ) -> !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 4, 5], f32> {
mo.graph @reshape_parametric_shape<D0, D1 -> D2, D3, D4>(
  %input: !mo.tensor<[D0, D1], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[D2, D3, D4], f32> {

  %param_shape = mosh.param.to_value: !mosh.ape = <[D0, 4, 5]>
  %target_shape = mo.shape.to_tensor(%param_shape) -> !mo.tensor<[3], si32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: kgen.param.declare {{.*}}: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"
  // CHECK-SAME:  {message = "[reshape] input and output number of elements must match:
  // CHECK-SAME: #mosh<ape[D0, D1]> : !mosh.ape != #mosh<ape[D0, 4, 5]> : !mosh.ape[[REST:.*]]" : !kgen.string},
  // CHECK-SAME: identical(:scalar<si64> mul_no_wrap(D0, D1), mul_no_wrap(D0, 20)))>
  //
  // CHECK-NEXT: %[[RES:.*]] = mo.static.reshape(%[[INPUT]])
  // CHECK-SAME:   : !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], [[D1]]], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 4, 5], f32>
  %res = mo.reshape<() -> D5, D6, D7>(%input, %target_shape) : (
    !mo.tensor<[D0, D1], f32>, !mo.tensor<[3], si32>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[D5, D6, D7], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output %[[RES]] : !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 4, 5], f32>
  mo.output<D5, D6, D7> %res : !mo.tensor<[D5, D6, D7], f32>
}

// COM: Makes sure we handle the case where we are reshaping scalar tensors
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph
// CHECK-SAME: @reshape_scalar_tensor([[VARG0:[^ ]*]]: !mo.tensor<[], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[1, 1, 1], f32> {
// CHECK-NEXT: [[V0:[^ ]*]] = mo.static.reshape([[VARG0]]) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[1, 1, 1], f32>
// CHECK-NEXT: mo.output [[V0]] : !mo.tensor<[1, 1, 1], f32>
mo.graph @reshape_scalar_tensor<() -> D2, D3, D4>(
  %input: !mo.tensor<[], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[D2, D3, D4], f32> {

  %param_shape = mosh.param.to_value: !mosh.ape = <[1, 1, 1]>
  %target_shape = mo.shape.to_tensor(%param_shape) -> !mo.tensor<[3], si32>
  %res = mo.reshape<() -> D5, D6, D7>(%input, %target_shape) : (
    !mo.tensor<[], f32>, !mo.tensor<[3], si32>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[D5, D6, D7], f32>

  mo.output<D5, D6, D7> %res : !mo.tensor<[D5, D6, D7], f32>
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @fold_abs_on_non_negative_dim
//  CHECK-SAME:  <[[D0:.*]]>(
mo.graph @fold_abs_on_non_negative_dim<D0 -> D1>(
  %dummy: !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>,
  %scalar: !mo.tensor<[], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[D1], f32> {

  // CHECK-NEXT: %[[RESULT:.*]] = mo.static.broadcast_to{{.*}} -> !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>
  kgen.param.declare D2: scalar<si64> = <cond(ge(:scalar<si64> D0, 0), D0, mul_no_wrap(D0, -1))>
  %result = mo.static.broadcast_to(%scalar) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[D2], f32>

  // CHECK-NEXT: mo.output %[[RESULT]]
  mo.output<D2> %result : !mo.tensor<[D2], f32>
}

// This test case is extracted from ONNX text encoder.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @select_fold_during_staticization
//  CHECK-SAME:   <[[SEQ_LEN:.*]], [[BATCH_SIZE:.*]]>(
//  CHECK-SAME:   [[INPUT:%.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[SEQ_LEN:.*]], [[BATCH_SIZE:.*]]], si32>
mo.graph @select_fold_during_staticization<seq_len, batch_size -> O1, O2>(
  %input: !mo.tensor<[seq_len, batch_size], si32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[O1, O2], si32> {

  %zero = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0> : tensor<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %zeros = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0, 0> : !M.array<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %one = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1> : tensor<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>

  // Essentially constructing `%target_shape` to represent
  //   `[0 == 0 ? seq_len : 0,  batch_size == 0 ? batch_size : batch_size]
  // which folds to
  //   `[seq_len, batch_size]`
  %input_shape = mo.shape_of(%input) : (!mo.tensor<[seq_len, batch_size], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %batch_size = mo.gather(%input_shape, %one) [axis = 0] : (!mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[1], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %zero_and_batch_size = mo.concat[0] (%zero, %batch_size) : (!mo.tensor<[1], si64>, !mo.tensor<[1], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %cond = mo.equal(%zero_and_batch_size, %zeros) : (!mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], bool>
  %target_shape = mo.select(%cond, %input_shape, %zero_and_batch_size) : (!mo.tensor<[2], bool>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si64>

  // reshape(%input, [seq_len, batch_size]) == %input
  %res = mo.reshape<() -> D1, D2>(%input, %target_shape) : (
    !mo.tensor<[seq_len, batch_size], si32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[D1, D2], si32>

  // CHECK: mo.output [[INPUT]]
  mo.output<D1, D2> %res : !mo.tensor<[D1, D2], si32>
}

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @range_gather
//  CHECK-SAME:   <[[N1:.*]], [[N2:.*]], [[N3:.*]]>(
//  CHECK-SAME:   [[INPUT:%.*]]: !mo.tensor<[], si32>
mo.graph @range_gather<N1, N2, N3 -> O1, O2>(
  %input: !mo.tensor<[], si32>,
  %dummy: !mo.tensor<[N1, N2, N3], si32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[O1, O2], si32> {

  %one = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1> : tensor<si32>> : !mo.tensor<[], si32>
  %dummy_shape = mo.shape_of(%dummy) : (!mo.tensor<[N1, N2, N3], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[3], si32>
  %three_idx = mosh.param.to_value = <3>
  %three = mo.index.to_tensor(%three_idx) -> !mo.tensor<[], si32>
  %range = mo.range(%one, %three, %one) : (!mo.tensor<[], si32>, !mo.tensor<[], si32>, !mo.tensor<[], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si32>
  %shape = mo.gather(%dummy_shape, %range) [axis = 0] : (!mo.tensor<[3], si32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si32>

  // CHECK: [[RES:%.*]] = mo.static.broadcast_to([[INPUT]]) : {{.*}} -> !mo.tensor<[[[N2]], [[N3]]], si32>
  %res = mo.broadcast_to<() -> D1, D2>(%input, %shape) : (!mo.tensor<[], si32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[D1, D2], si32>

  // CHECK: mo.output [[RES]]
  mo.output<D1, D2> %res : !mo.tensor<[D1, D2], si32>
}

// This test ensures that staticized input actually gets materialized via
// `mo.shape.to_tensor`, so that we don't have to run all the shape computation
// via kernels. This is important for ops which can be shape inferred and have
// non-trivial data dependent input.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @slice_with_staticized_input
//  CHECK-SAME: <[[D0:.*]]>(
//  CHECK-SAME: [[INPUT:%.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 2304], f32>
//   CHECK-DAG:   [[STEP:%.*]] = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 1> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
//   CHECK-DAG:   [[START:%.*]] = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0, 768> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
//   CHECK-DAG:   [[STOP_MOSH:%.*]] = mosh.param.to_value: !mosh.ape = <[[[D0]], 1536]>
//  CHECK-NEXT:   [[STOP:%.*]] = mo.shape.to_tensor([[STOP_MOSH]]) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
//  CHECK-NEXT:   [[RES:%.*]] = mo.slice([[INPUT]], [[START]], [[STOP]], [[STEP]]) : {{.*}} -> !mo.tensor<[D0, 768], f32>
//  CHECK-NEXT:   mo.output [[RES]]
mo.graph @slice_with_staticized_input<D0 -> D1, D2>(
  %input: !mo.tensor<[D0, 2304], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[D1, D2], f32> {
  %step = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 1> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %two = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<2> : tensor<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %zero = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0> : !M.array<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %neg_one = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<-1> : tensor<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %three = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<3> : tensor<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>

  // The following is a generic way to compute N // 3 (where N == 2304 in our
  // case). It can't be constant folded because `mo.shape_of(%input)` isn't a
  // constant op as it's formulated (the 1st input dimension is dynamic).
  %in_shape = mo.shape_of(%input) : (!mo.tensor<[D0, 2304], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %last_dim = mo.gather(%in_shape, %neg_one) [axis = 0] : (!mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[1], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %add = mo.add(%last_dim, %two) : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %div = mo.div(%add, %three) : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %mul = mo.mul(%div, %two) : !mo.tensor<[1], si64>

  // Prepare the start/stop bounds.
  %d0 = mo.gather(%in_shape, %zero) [axis = 0] : (!mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[1], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[1], si64>
  %start = mo.concat[0] (%zero, %div) : (!mo.tensor<[1], si64>, !mo.tensor<[1], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %stop = mo.concat[0] (%d0, %mul) : (!mo.tensor<[1], si64>, !mo.tensor<[1], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si64>

  %res = mo.slice<() -> D3, D4>(%input, %start, %stop, %step) : (!mo.tensor<[D0, 2304], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[D3, D4], f32>
  mo.output<D3, D4> %res : !mo.tensor<[D3, D4], f32>
}

// Ensure shape computations related in a general slice operation are
// propagated.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @slice
// CHECK:       (%[[ARG0:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[1], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], si32>
// CHECK:       %[[OUT:.*]] = mo.static.broadcast_to(%[[ARG0]]) : !mo.tensor<[1], si32> -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], si32>
// CHECK:       mo.output %[[OUT]] : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], si32>
mo.graph @slice<() -> O0, O1>(%arg0: !mo.tensor<[1], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[O0, O1], si32> {
  %0 = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 1> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %1 = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0> : !M.array<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[], si64>
  %c2 = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<2, 2> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %c3 = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<3, 3> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>

  %ones = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1, 1> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>
  %zeros = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0, 0> : tensor<2xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[2], si64>

  %6 = mo.greater(%zeros, %ones) : (!mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], bool>
  %7 = mo.not(%6) : !mo.tensor<[2], bool>
  %8 = mo.select(%7, %c2, %c3) : (!mo.tensor<[2], bool>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[2], si64>

  %out = mo.broadcast_to<() -> D0, D1>(%arg0, %8) : (!mo.tensor<[1], si32>, !mo.tensor<[2], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[D0, D1], si32>
  mo.output<D0, D1> %out : !mo.tensor<[D0, D1], si32>
}

// This test ensures we can shape infer through a `mo.concat` op with non-equal
// dimensions (i.e., it doesn't rely on shape inference being able to prove the
// dimensions are equal). This is important because sometimes we can't prove as
// much as we want, but we still want to shape infer through `mo.concat`, which
// is an important op for shape inference in models like transformer.
mo.graph @concat_non_equal_dims<D10, D11, D12, D13, D14, D15>(%arg0: !mo.tensor<[D10, 1, D11], f32>, %arg1: !mo.tensor<[D12, 2, D13], f32>, %arg2: !mo.tensor<[D14, 3, D15], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[D10, 6, D11], f32> {
    %0 = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1> : tensor<si64>> : !mo.tensor<[], si64>
    kgen.param.declare assert20: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"{message = "[concat] input shapes must match except at concat axis" : !kgen.string}, eq(:!kgen.scalar<si64> D10, D12))>
    kgen.param.declare assert22: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"{message = "[concat] input shapes must match except at concat axis" : !kgen.string}, eq(:!kgen.scalar<si64> D11, D13))>
    kgen.param.declare assert24: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"{message = "[concat] input shapes must match except at concat axis" : !kgen.string}, eq(:!kgen.scalar<si64> D10, D14))>
    kgen.param.declare assert26: !mo.chain = <apply(:(!kgen.scalar<bool>) -> !mo.chain "mo.assert"{message = "[concat] input shapes must match except at concat axis" : !kgen.string}, eq(:!kgen.scalar<si64> D11, D15))>
    %1 = mo.concat[1] (%arg0, %arg1, %arg2) : (!mo.tensor<[D10, 1, D11], f32>, !mo.tensor<[D12, 2, D13], f32>, !mo.tensor<[D14, 3, D15], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[D10, 6, D11], f32>
    mo.output %1 : !mo.tensor<[D10, 6, D11], f32>
}
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph
// CHECK-SAME: @concat_non_equal_dims<[[D0:.*]], [[D1:.*]], [[D2:.*]], [[D3:.*]], [[D4:.*]], [[D5:.*]]>([[INPUT1:%.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 1, [[D1]]], f32>, [[INPUT2:%.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D2]], 2, [[D3]]], f32>, [[INPUT3:%.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D4]], 3, [[D5]]], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 6, [[D1]]], f32> {
// CHECK-NEXT:   {{.*}}"mo.assert"{{.*}} "[concat] input shapes must match except at concat axis" {{.*}} identical(:scalar<si64> [[D0]], [[D2]])
// CHECK-NEXT:   {{.*}}"mo.assert"{{.*}} "[concat] input shapes must match except at concat axis" {{.*}} identical(:scalar<si64> [[D1]], [[D3]])
// CHECK-NEXT:   {{.*}}"mo.assert"{{.*}} "[concat] input shapes must match except at concat axis" {{.*}} identical(:scalar<si64> [[D0]], [[D4]])
// CHECK-NEXT:   {{.*}}"mo.assert"{{.*}} "[concat] input shapes must match except at concat axis" {{.*}} identical(:scalar<si64> [[D1]], [[D5]])
// CHECK-NEXT:   [[RES:%.*]] = mo.concat{{.*}}([[INPUT1]], [[INPUT2]], [[INPUT3]]) : {{.*}} -> !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], 6, [[D1]]], f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:   mo.output [[RES]]
// CHECK-NEXT: }

// regression test to make sure we can staticize `mo.negative`.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @staticize_mo_negative
//  CHECK-SAME:  <[[D0:.*]], [[D1:.*]], [[D2:.*]], [[D3:.*]]>(
//  CHECK-SAME:  %[[INPUT:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[D0]], [[D1]], [[D2]], [[D3]]], bf16>
//       CHECK:  %[[RES:.*]] = mo.range{{.*}} -> !mo.tensor<[[[D2]]], si64>
//  CHECK-NEXT:  mo.output{{.*}} %[[RES:.*]]
mo.graph @staticize_mo_negative<D0, D1, D2, D3>(%arg0: !mo.tensor<[D0, D1, D2, D3], bf16>) -> !mo.tensor<[D2], si64> {
    %0 = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0> : !M.array<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[], si64>
    %1 = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<-1> : tensor<1xsi64>> : !mo.tensor<[], si64>
    %2 = mosh.param.to_value = <mul_no_wrap(D2, -1)>
    %3 = mo.index.to_tensor(%2) -> !mo.tensor<[], si64>
    %4 = mo.range(%0, %3, %1) : (!mo.tensor<[], si64>, !mo.tensor<[], si64>, !mo.tensor<[], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[D2], si64>
    mo.output %4 : !mo.tensor<[D2], si64>
}

// RUN: mo-opt --split-input-file --verify-diagnostics --mo-validate-devices="default-device-target-triple=arm64-apple-darwin23.6.0 default-device-target-arch=aarch64" --gc-pipeline %s

// RUN: mo-opt --split-input-file --verify-diagnostics --mo-validate-devices="default-device-target-triple=x86_64-unknown-linux default-device-target-arch=x86_64" --gc-pipeline %s

mo.graph @cast<dim>(%arg0: !mo.tensor<[dim], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[dim], f8e5m2> attributes {argument_names = ["input0"], result_names = ["output0"]} {
  %0 = mo.chain.create()
  // expected-error @below {{The f8e5m2 data type is not supported on device 'cpu:0'.}}
  %1 = mo.cast(%arg0) { device_ref = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0> } : (!mo.tensor<[dim], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[dim], f8e5m2>
  mo.output %1 : !mo.tensor<[dim], f8e5m2>
}

// -----

// expected-error @below {{The f8e5m2 data type is not supported on device 'cpu:0'.}}
mo.graph @cast<dim>(%arg0: !mo.tensor<[dim], f8e5m2>) -> !mo.tensor<[dim], f32> attributes {argument_names = ["input0"], result_names = ["output0"]} {
  %0 = mo.chain.create()
  %1 = mo.cast(%arg0) { device_ref = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0> } : (!mo.tensor<[dim], f8e5m2>) -> !mo.tensor<[dim], f32>
  mo.output %1 : !mo.tensor<[dim], f32>
}

// RUN: mo-opt -mo-shape-inference -mo-symbolic-optimize -mo-pattern-fusion %s | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CHECK-IR

// CHECK-IR: mo.graph @tf_layer_norm(%[[ARG0:.*]]:  !mo.tensor<[4, 3, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 3, 2], f32>
mo.graph @tf_layer_norm(%arg0 : !mo.tensor<[4, 3, 2], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[4, 3, 2], f32>) {
  // CHECK-IR: %[[EPS:.*]] = mo.constant {{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[], f32>
  // CHECK-IR: %[[GAM:.*]] = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1.100{{.*}}> : !mo.tensor<[2], f32>
  // CHECK-IR: %[[BET:.*]] = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<-1.000{{.*}}> : !mo.tensor<[2], f32>
  // CHECK-IR: %[[VAL1:.*]] = mo.reduce.layer_norm(%[[ARG0]], %[[GAM]], %[[BET]], %[[EPS]])
  // CHECK-IR: mo.output %[[VAL1]]
  %sh = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<4, 3, 2> : tensor<3xsi64>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[3], si64>
  %sh2 = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<4, 3, 1> : tensor<3xsi64>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[3], si64>
  %eps = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<0.00001> : tensor<f32>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[], f32>
  %gamma = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<1.1, 2.1> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[2], f32>
  %beta = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<-1.0, -2.0> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[2], f32>

// A wide last dim lets fast-math rewrite the division by sqrt into a
// multiplication by rsqrt before fusion; the pattern must still fuse.
// CHECK-IR: mo.graph @pt_layer_norm_wide<[[B:.*]]>(%[[ARG0:.*]]: !mo.tensor<[[[B]], 3, 16], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[[[B]], 3, 16], f32>
mo.graph @pt_layer_norm_wide<B>(%arg0 : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>) {
  // CHECK-IR: %[[EPS:.*]] = mo.constant {{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[], f32>

  // CHECK-IR: mo.output %[[VAL1]]
  %eps = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<0.00001> : tensor<f32>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[], f32>
  %gamma = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<1.1, 2.1, 1.1, 2.1, 1.1, 2.1, 1.1, 2.1, 1.1, 2.1, 1.1, 2.1, 1.1, 2.1, 1.1, 2.1> : tensor<16xf32>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[16], f32>
  %beta = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<-1.0, -2.0, -1.0, -2.0, -1.0, -2.0, -1.0, -2.0, -1.0, -2.0, -1.0, -2.0, -1.0, -2.0, -1.0, -2.0> : tensor<16xf32>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[16], f32>
  %v1_sum = mo.reduce.add(%arg0) : (!mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %v1_len = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<16.0> : tensor<1xf32>> : !mo.tensor<[], f32>
  %v1_len_b = mo.static.broadcast_to(%v1_len) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %1 = mo.div(%v1_sum, %v1_len_b) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %2 = mo.static.broadcast_to(%1) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  %3 = mo.sub(%arg0, %2) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  %4 = mo.mul(%3, %3) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  %v5_sum = mo.reduce.add(%4) : (!mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %v5_len = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<16.0> : tensor<1xf32>> : !mo.tensor<[], f32>
  %v5_len_b = mo.static.broadcast_to(%v5_len) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %5 = mo.div(%v5_sum, %v5_len_b) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %6 = mo.static.broadcast_to(%eps) : !mo.tensor<[], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %7 = mo.add(%5, %6) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %8 = mo.sqrt(%7) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32>
  %9 = mo.static.broadcast_to(%8) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 1], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  %10 = mo.div(%3, %9) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  %11 = mo.static.broadcast_to(%gamma) : !mo.tensor<[16], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  %12 = mo.mul(%10, %11) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  %13 = mo.static.broadcast_to(%beta) : !mo.tensor<[16], f32> -> !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  %14 = mo.add(%12, %13) : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
  mo.output %14 : !mo.tensor<[B, 3, 16], f32>
}

// CHECK-IR-LABEL: mo.graph @pt_layer_norm_folded_reciprocal_f16
// CHECK-IR:       mo.reduce.layer_norm
mo.graph @pt_layer_norm_folded_reciprocal_f16(%arg0 : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>) -> (!mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>) {
  %sh = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<4, 2, 3> : tensor<3xsi64>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[3], si64>
  %sh2 = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<4, 2, 1> : tensor<3xsi64>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[3], si64>
  %eps = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<0.00001> : tensor<f16>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[], f16>
  %gamma = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<1.1, 2.1, 3.1> : tensor<3xf16>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[3], f16>
  %beta = "mo.constant"() {value = #M.dense_array<-1.0, -2.0, -3.0> : tensor<3xf16>} : () -> !mo.tensor<[3], f16>
  %v1_sum = mo.reduce.add(%arg0) : (!mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %v1_len = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0.333251953125> : tensor<1xf16>> : !mo.tensor<[], f16>
  %v1_len_b = mo.static.broadcast_to(%v1_len) : !mo.tensor<[], f16> -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %1 = mo.mul(%v1_sum, %v1_len_b) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %2 = mo.broadcast_to(%1, %sh) : (!mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>, !mo.tensor<[3], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  %3 = mo.sub(%arg0, %2) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  %4 = mo.mul(%3, %3) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  %v5_sum = mo.reduce.add(%4) : (!mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %v5_len = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<0.333251953125> : tensor<1xf16>> : !mo.tensor<[], f16>
  %v5_len_b = mo.static.broadcast_to(%v5_len) : !mo.tensor<[], f16> -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %5 = mo.mul(%v5_sum, %v5_len_b) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %6 = mo.broadcast_to(%eps, %sh2) : (!mo.tensor<[], f16>, !mo.tensor<[3], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %7 = mo.add(%5, %6) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %8 = mo.sqrt(%7) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>
  %9 = mo.broadcast_to(%8, %sh) : (!mo.tensor<[4, 2, 1], f16>, !mo.tensor<[3], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  %10 = mo.div(%3, %9) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  %11 = mo.broadcast_to(%gamma, %sh) : (!mo.tensor<[3], f16>, !mo.tensor<[3], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  %12 = mo.mul(%10, %11) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  %13 = mo.broadcast_to(%beta, %sh) : (!mo.tensor<[3], f16>, !mo.tensor<[3], si64>) -> !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  %14 = mo.add(%12, %13) : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
  mo.output %14 : !mo.tensor<[4, 2, 3], f16>
}

#include "Mojo/KGENDialect/KGENOps.h"
#include "Mojo/KGENDialect/KGENParameters.h"
#include "Mojo/KGENDialect/ParameterEvaluator.h"
#include "Mojo/LITDialect/LITUtils.h"
#include "Mojo/Support/CompilerProfiling.h"
#include "Mojo/ToolCommon/KGENPasses.h"
#include "Support/Compiler/OperationUtils.h"
#include "Support/Compiler/Threading.h"
#include "mlir/Analysis/SymbolTableAnalysis.h"
#include "mlir/IR/BuiltinOps.h"
#include "mlir/IR/PatternMatch.h"
#include "mlir/IR/Threading.h"
#include "mlir/Pass/Pass.h"
#include "llvm/Support/Mutex.h"

using namespace M;
using namespace KGEN;

namespace M::KGEN {
#define GEN_PASS_DEF_VERIFYPARAMETERS
#include "Mojo/KGENPasses.h.inc"
} // namespace M::KGEN

/// Function to walk all op users of parameters and substitute parameters based
/// on the values currently in the evaluator.
static void processOp(Operation *op, ParameterEvaluator &evaluator) {
  SmallVector<NamedAttribute> attrs;
  bool changed = false;
  for (const NamedAttribute &attr : op->getAttrs()) {
    Attribute newAttr = evaluator.getReboundAttribute(attr.getValue());
    attrs.emplace_back(attr.getName(), newAttr);
    changed |= newAttr != attr.getValue();
  }
  if (changed)
    op->setAttrs(DictionaryAttr::getWithSorted(op->getContext(), attrs));

  for (OpResult result : op->getResults())
    result.setType(evaluator.getReboundType(result.getType()));
  for (Region &region : op->getRegions())
    for (BlockArgument arg : region.getArguments())
      arg.setType(evaluator.getReboundType(arg.getType()));
}

/// Propagate trivial parameter declarations in the region, given the use-def
/// graph for that region and the top-level graph to lookup nested regions.
static void propagateTrivialParameters(Region *region,
                                       const ParameterUseDefGraph &graph,
                                       const ParameterUseDefGraph &topLevel,
                                       ParameterEvaluator evaluator) {
  // Collect the defining operations in topological order. The same operation
  // can define multiple parameters, so punt them according to their most
  // dominated definition. Do this by collecting them in reverse.
  llvm::SetVector<Operation *> defOps;
  for (StringAttr param : llvm::reverse(graph.params))
    defOps.insert(graph.defs.at(param).defOp);
  for (Operation *op : llvm::reverse(defOps)) {
    if (auto decl = dyn_cast<DeclInterface>(op);
        decl && op == region->getParentOp()) {
      // For parent decl ops, bind input parameters to themselves.
      for (ParamDeclAttr decl : decl.getInputParams()) {
        decl = cast<ParamDeclAttr>(evaluator.getReboundAttribute(decl));
        evaluator.setDeclBinding(decl, ParamDeclRefAttr::get(decl));
      }
      // All required parameters are bound for the parent op. Process it now.
      // Skip the top-level declaration since it cannot reference parameters
      // declared inside it.
      if (op != topLevel.scope->getParentOp())
        processOp(op, evaluator);
    } else if (auto declare = dyn_cast<ParamDeclareOp>(op)) {
      // If the value of the declared parameter is "trivial", i.e. a simple
      // constant, then propagate it. We can only safely refine the attribute
      // (interpret calls) if its type is not parametric. If the type is
      // parametric, we risk creating unequal types across function calls if
      // there are dependent parameters.
      TypedAttr value = declare.getValue();
      if (!isa<DeferredAttr>(value))
        value = evaluator.getReboundAttribute(value);

      // The type of the parameter may change. Try to rebind it.
      auto decl = cast<ParamDeclAttr>(
          evaluator.getReboundAttribute(declare.getParamDecl()));
      evaluator.setDeclBinding(decl, value);
      declare.erase();
    } else {
      // If this is any other operation, just walk its definitions in the
      // current scope.
      cast<ParamOpInterface>(op).walkDefinitions(
          [&](ParamDeclAttr decl, const ParamDefValue &value) {
            decl = cast<ParamDeclAttr>(evaluator.getReboundAttribute(decl));
            evaluator.setDeclBinding(decl, ParamDeclRefAttr::get(decl));
          });
      processOp(op, evaluator);
    }
  }

  for (Operation *op : graph.paramOps) {
    processOp(op, evaluator);

    // Peephole rebinds that have been resolved to the same types.
    if (auto rebind = dyn_cast<RebindOp>(op);
        rebind && rebind.getInput().getType() == rebind.getType()) {
      rebind.replaceAllUsesWith(rebind.getInput());
      rebind.erase();
      continue;
    }

    // GeneratorUser ops need concretize callee to be called when the callee
    // attr is updated.
    if (auto generatorUser = dyn_cast<GeneratorUserOpInterface>(op)) {
      if (auto symCst =
              dyn_cast<SymbolConstantAttr>(generatorUser.getCallee())) {
        IRRewriter b{OpBuilder(op)};
        generatorUser.concretizeCallee(b, symCst);
      }
    }
  }

  // Any op might contain a parametric location, so we go through all of them.
  auto rebindLoc = [&](Location loc) {
    return cast<Location>(evaluator.getReboundAttribute(loc));
  };
  OpRegionBlockWalker walker(
      [&](Operation *op) {
        if (auto inlined = dyn_cast<DebugInfo::InlinedSubprogramScoped>(op))
          if (LocationAttr loc = inlined.getCallLocAttr())
            inlined.setCallLocAttr(rebindLoc(loc));
        // DeclInterface's location might reference parameters declared by it
        // (e.g. in case of a parametric argument making it into a subprogram
        // scope type), so we will handle it when we recurse into it.
        if (isa<DeclInterface>(op))
          return WalkResult::skip();
        op->setLoc(rebindLoc(op->getLoc()));
        return WalkResult::advance();
      },
      nullptr,
      [&](Block *block) {
        for (BlockArgument arg : block->getArguments())
          arg.setLoc(rebindLoc(arg.getLoc()));
        return WalkResult::advance();
      });
  walker.walk(region);
  // Don't process the top-level decl operation. It cannot reference
  // declarations in its body and its location is shared across threads.
  if (region->getParentOp() != topLevel.scope->getParentOp())
    if (auto declScope = dyn_cast<DeclInterface>(region->getParentOp()))
      declScope->setLoc(rebindLoc(declScope->getLoc()));

  // Recurse into nested parameter scopes.
  for (Region *region : graph.nestedDecls) {
    propagateTrivialParameters(region, topLevel.nestedScopes.at(region),
                               topLevel, evaluator);
  }
}

namespace {
struct VerifyParametersPass : impl::VerifyParametersBase<VerifyParametersPass> {
  using VerifyParametersBase::VerifyParametersBase;

  void runOnOperation() override {
    using ParamCache = ParameterCollector::Analysis;

    auto &analysis = getAnalysis<mlir::SymbolTableAnalysis>();
    mlir::LockedSymbolTableCollection sharedSymtabs(analysis.getSymbolTables());
    auto &paramCache = getAnalysis<ParamCache>();
    bool emptyCache = paramCache.parameterLess.empty();

    std::vector<std::pair<Region *, size_t>> declRegions;
    ModuleOp module = getOperation();
    for (auto decl : module.getOps<DeclInterface>())
      for (Region &region : decl->getRegions())
        declRegions.emplace_back(&region, declRegions.size());

    LIT::LITSymTabEvaluationContext evaluationContext(module, sharedSymtabs);

    // Because parameter simplification invokes the interpreter, we cannot
    // simplify in parallel: functions may be modified as they are being
    // interpreted. Save the use-def graphs from the verification pass here.
    std::vector<ParameterUseDefGraph> graphs;
    if (simplifyParameters) {
      graphs.reserve(declRegions.size());
      for (size_t i = 0, e = declRegions.size(); i != e; ++i)
        graphs.emplace_back(nullptr);
    }

    auto workFunc =
        [&evaluationContext, &graphs, simplify = bool(simplifyParameters)](
            ParamCache &paramCache, std::pair<Region *, size_t> item) {
          auto [declRegion, i] = item;
          ParameterUseDefGraph graph(*declRegion);
          if (failed(graph.verify(&evaluationContext, paramCache)))
            return failure();
          if (simplify)
            graphs[i] = std::move(graph);
          return mlir::success();
        };

    auto consolidateFn = [emptyCache](ParamCache &original,
                                      ArrayRef<ParamCache> threadCaches) {
      // Consolidate the caches, but only when the original cache is empty.
      // In reality, the cache does not grow much after the first run of
      // this pass on an input IR, so consolidation is only worthwhile on
      // the first run of the pass, when the cache is empty.
      if (emptyCache)
        return;
      for (const ParamCache &threadCache : threadCaches) {
        original.parameterLess.insert(threadCache.parameterLess.begin(),
                                      threadCache.parameterLess.end());
      }
    };

    if (failed(failableParallelForEach(&getContext(), declRegions,
                                       std::move(workFunc), paramCache,
                                       consolidateFn)))
      return signalPassFailure();

    // This pass does not modify any IR, so mark all analyses as preserved. In
    // addition, this signals the pass manager that the MLIR verifier need not
    // run after this pass.
    if (!simplifyParameters) {
      markAllAnalysesPreserved();
      return;
    }

    VerboseCompilerTimeTraceScope traceScope("propagateTrivialParameters");
    for (auto [declRegion, i] : declRegions) {
      ParameterUseDefGraph &graph = graphs[i];
      ParameterEvaluator evaluator;
      evaluator.setEvaluationContext(&evaluationContext);
      propagateTrivialParameters(declRegion, graph, graph,
                                 std::move(evaluator));
    }
  }
};
} // namespace

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from max.driver import CPU, Accelerator, Buffer, accelerator_count
from max.dtype import DType
from max.engine.api import InferenceSession
from max.graph import DeviceRef, Graph, TensorType, ops


def main() -> None:
    mojo_kernels = Path(__file__).parent / "kernels"

    dtype = DType.float32

    # Place the graph on a GPU, if available. Fall back to CPU if not.
    device = CPU() if accelerator_count() == 0 else Accelerator()
    if accelerator_count() == 0:
        N = 8
        D = 8
        BD = 4
        BN = 4
    else:
        N = 32
        D = 32
        BD = 8
        BN = 16

    with Graph(
        "fused_attention",
        input_types=[
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
        ],
        custom_extensions=[mojo_kernels],
    ) as graph:
        q, k, v, *_ = graph.inputs
        results = ops.custom(
            name="modular_ops::fused_attention_custom",
            device=DeviceRef.from_device(device),
            parameters={"BD": BD, "BN": BN},
            values=[q, k, v],
            out_types=[
                TensorType(
                    dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
                )
            ],
        )
        graph.output(*results)

    # Set up an inference session for running the graph.
    session = InferenceSession(devices=[device])

    # Compile the graph.
    compiled = session.compile(graph)
    model = session.init(compiled)

    np.random.seed(123)
    Q = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
    K = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
    V = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)

    output = model.execute(Q, K, V)
    print(output)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
The code below computes the attention score for a tile of size BN x BD.
It follows the exact arithmetic as described in the FlashAttention-2 paper
(https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08691). The variable names in this program
reflect the variable names in the algorithms from the paper.

Here, the following tensors are Q for the query,
K for the key, V for the value, and O for the output.

       Q            K               V
  +----D----+  +----D----+   +--+--BD--+---+
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |.........|  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  BN........|  N.........|   N  |......|   |
  |.........|  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  +---------+   +--+------+---+

The main trick is in the softmax computation.
As the paper says, S and P are intermediate values.

Let S = Q * K^T  ∈ R^{N, D}
    P = Softmax(S) ∈ R^{N, D}
The attention score is O = P * V ∈ R^{N, D}.

One way to think about this is to consider what happens if we
split the dimensions N in  K, and Q into two tiles: K_1 and K_2, V_1 and V_2.
Then we can incrementally compute the output as follows:
  S_1 = Q * K_1, S_2 = Q * K_2
  O_i = O_{i-1} * renormalization_factor + softmax(S_i) * V_i

This allows for the incremental computation of softmax(S_i) * V_i,
leading to the final output.
"""


from max.gpu.host import DeviceContext
from max.gpu import block_idx
from max.gpu.sync import barrier
from layout import TensorLayout, TileTensor, row_major, stack_allocation
from layout.math import max, sum
from layout.tensor_core import TensorCore

from extensibility import register, InputTensor, OutputTensor

from std.utils import Index


@register("modular_ops::fused_attention_custom")
struct FusedAttention:
    """Registers the `fused_attention_custom` op, allowing python to use it from the `max`
    package.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        rank: Int,
        //,  # Forces the previous two params to be inferred from the args
        BN: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split Q into
        BD: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split K, V into
        target: StaticString,  # "cpu" or "gpu"
    ](
        output: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        query: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        key: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        value: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime assert rank == 2, "rank must be 2"

        # Query tensor
        var Q = query.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Key tensor
        var K = key.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Value tensor
        var V = value.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Attention output tensor
        var O = output.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()

        comptime if target == "cpu":
            print("Running on CPU")
            fused_attention_cpu[BN, BD](Q, K, V, O)
        else:
            var dev_ctx = ctx
            print("Running on GPU")
            fused_attention_gpu[BN, BD](dev_ctx, Q, K, V, O)


# CustomOpLibrary does not support names with '::' in them currently. Create
# a simple alias so the whisper example works.
@register("fused_attention_custom")
struct FusedAttentionAlias:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        rank: Int,
        //,  # Forces the previous two params to be inferred from the args
        BN: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split Q into
        BD: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split K, V into
        target: StaticString,  # "cpu" or "gpu"
    ](
        output: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        query: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        key: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        value: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        FusedAttention.execute[BN=BN, BD=BD, target=target](
            output, query, key, value, ctx
        )


@inline(.always)
def matmul_b_transpose(
    lhs: TileTensor,
    rhs: TileTensor,
    out res: TileTensor[
        lhs.dtype,
        type_of(row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()),
        MutUntrackedOrigin,
    ],
):
    res = stack_allocation[lhs.dtype](
        row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()
    )

    comptime for m in range(lhs.static_shape[0]):
        comptime for n in range(rhs.static_shape[0]):
            res[m, n] = 0.0

            comptime for k in range(lhs.static_shape[1]):
                res[m, n] += rebind[res.ElementType](
                    lhs[m, k].cast[res.dtype]()
                ) * rebind[res.ElementType](rhs[n, k].cast[res.dtype]())


# The bulk of the code below implements what the papers calls
# an "online softmax", which is local to each block.
# The algorithm is described as:
#
# $$$
# m_1 = rowmax(S_1)
# l_1 = rowsum(e^(S_1-m_1))
# P_1 = diag(l_1)^-1 * e^(S_1-m_1)
# O_1 = P_1*V_1 = diag(l_1)^-1 * e^(S_1-m_1) * V_1
# m_2 = max(m_1, rowmax(S_2)) = m
# l_2 = e^(m_1-m_2) * l_1 _ rowsum(e^(S_2-m_2))
#     = rowsum(e^(S_1-m)) + rowsum(e^(S_2-m)) = ls
# P_2 = diag(l_2)^-1 * e^(S_2-m_2)
# O_2 = diag(l_1/l_2)^-1 * O_1 + (P_2 * V_2)
#     = diag(l_2)^-1 * e^(S_2-m) * V
# $$$


@inline(.always)
def fused_attention_cpu[
    BN: Int, BD: Int
](Q: TileTensor, K: TileTensor, V: TileTensor, O: TileTensor[mut=True, ...],):
    comptime N = K.static_shape[0]
    comptime D = K.static_shape[1]

    comptime for tile_n in range(N // BN):
        var Q_tile = Q.tile[BN, D](tile_n, 0)

        comptime for tile_d in range(D // BD):
            var m_1 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(
                Scalar[Q.dtype].MIN
            )

            var l_1 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(0)

            var O_i = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN, BD]()).fill(0)

            comptime for tile_n_idx in range(N // BN):
                var K_tile = K.tile[BN, D](tile_n_idx, 0)
                var V_tile = V.tile[BN, BD](tile_n_idx, tile_d)

                var S = matmul_b_transpose(Q_tile, K_tile)
                var m_2 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                max[axis=1](S, m_2)
                m_2.max(m_1)

                # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
                var l_2 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                l_2.copy_from(m_1)
                l_2 -= m_2
                l_2.exp()
                l_2 *= l_1
                var E = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN, BN]())
                E.copy_from(S)
                E -= m_2
                E.exp()
                var l_2_sum = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                sum[axis=1](E, l_2_sum)
                l_2 += l_2_sum

                # P = exp(S - m_2) / l_2
                E /= l_2
                O_i *= l_1
                O_i /= l_2
                var m_1_delta = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                m_1_delta.copy_from(m_1)
                m_1_delta -= m_2
                m_1_delta.exp()
                O_i *= m_1_delta
                var PV = matmul["cpu"](E, V_tile)
                O_i += PV
                m_1.copy_from(m_2)
                l_1.copy_from(l_2)

            O.tile[BN, BD](tile_n, tile_d).copy_from(O_i)


@inline(.always)
def matmul[
    dtype: DType,
    rhs_dtype: DType,
    //,
    target: StaticString,
    transpose_b: Bool = False,
](
    lhs: TileTensor[dtype, ...],
    rhs: TileTensor[rhs_dtype, ...],
    out res: TileTensor[
        dtype,
        type_of(row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()),
        MutUntrackedOrigin,
        address_space=lhs.address_space,
    ],
):
    res = stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=lhs.address_space](
        row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()
    )

    comptime if target == "cpu":
        comptime for m in range(lhs.static_shape[0]):
            comptime for n in range(rhs.static_shape[1]):
                res[m, n] = 0.0

                comptime for k in range(lhs.static_shape[1]):
                    res[m, n] += rebind[res.ElementType](
                        lhs[m, k].cast[res.dtype]()
                    ) * rebind[res.ElementType](rhs[k, n].cast[res.dtype]())
    else:
        comptime M = lhs.static_shape[0]
        comptime N = rhs.static_shape[0]
        comptime K = lhs.static_shape[1]

        var out_sram = stack_allocation[res.dtype, address_space=.SHARED](
            row_major[M, N]()
        )

        comptime BK = 8

        comptime assert K % 8 == 0, "K needs to be a multiple of 8"

        var mma_b_t = TensorCore[dtype, dtype, Index(M, N, BK), transpose_b]()

        var c_reg = stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=.LOCAL](
            mma_b_t.c_fragment_layout
        ).fill(0)

        # `TensorCore`'s native loads require matching operand dtypes;
        # rebind the B view once when `rhs` carries a different dtype.
        var rhs_typed = rebind[
            TileTensor[
                dtype,
                rhs.LayoutType,
                rhs.origin,
                Engine=rhs.Engine,
                address_space=rhs.address_space,
                linear_idx_type=rhs.linear_idx_type,
            ]
        ](rhs)

        comptime for k_i in range(K // BK):
            var a_reg = mma_b_t.load_a(lhs.tile[M, BK](0, k_i))

            var b_reg = mma_b_t.load_b(rhs_typed.tile[BK, N](k_i, 0))

            comptime if transpose_b:
                b_reg = rebind[type_of(b_reg)](
                    mma_b_t.load_b(rhs_typed.tile[N, BK](0, k_i))
                )

            var d_reg = mma_b_t.mma_op(a_reg, b_reg, c_reg)
            c_reg.copy_from(d_reg)
        mma_b_t.store_d(out_sram, c_reg)

        barrier()
        res.copy_from(out_sram)


def fused_attention_kernel[
    q_dtype: DType,
    q_layout: TensorLayout,
    k_dtype: DType,
    k_layout: TensorLayout,
    v_dtype: DType,
    v_layout: TensorLayout,
    o_dtype: DType,
    o_layout: TensorLayout,
    BN: Int,
    BD: Int,
](
    Q: TileTensor[q_dtype, q_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    K: TileTensor[k_dtype, k_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    V: TileTensor[v_dtype, v_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    O: TileTensor[o_dtype, o_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
):
    comptime N = Q.static_shape[0]
    comptime D = Q.static_shape[1]

    var Q_tile = Q.tile[BN, D](block_idx.y, 0)

    var m_1 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(
        Scalar[q_dtype].MIN
    )
    var l_1 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(0)
    var O_i = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN, BD]()).fill(0)

    comptime BN_1 = 8

    for tile_n_idx in range(N // BN_1):
        var K_tile = K.tile[BN_1, D](tile_n_idx, 0)
        var V_tile = V.tile[BN_1, BD](tile_n_idx, block_idx.x)
        var S = matmul["gpu", transpose_b=True](Q_tile, K_tile)
        var m_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        max[axis=1](S, m_2)
        m_2.max(m_1)

        # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
        var l_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        l_2.copy_from(m_1)
        l_2 -= m_2
        l_2.exp()
        l_2 *= l_1
        var E = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN, BN_1]())
        E.copy_from(S)
        E -= m_2
        E.exp()
        var l_2_sum = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        sum[axis=1](E, l_2_sum)
        l_2 += l_2_sum

        # P = exp(S - m_2) / l_2
        E /= l_2
        O_i *= l_1
        O_i /= l_2
        var m_1_delta = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        m_1_delta.copy_from(m_1)
        m_1_delta -= m_2
        m_1_delta.exp()
        O_i *= m_1_delta
        var PV = matmul["gpu"](E, V_tile)
        O_i += PV
        m_1.copy_from(m_2)
        l_1.copy_from(l_2)
    O.tile[BN, BD](block_idx.y, block_idx.x).copy_from(O_i)


def fused_attention_gpu[
    BN: Int,
    BD: Int,
](
    ctx: DeviceContext,
    Q: TileTensor,
    K: TileTensor,
    V: TileTensor,
    O: TileTensor[mut=True, ...],
) raises:
    comptime kernel_func = fused_attention_kernel[
        Q.dtype,
        Q.LayoutType,
        K.dtype,
        K.LayoutType,
        V.dtype,
        V.LayoutType,
        O.dtype,
        O.LayoutType,
        BN,
        BD,
    ]
    ctx.enqueue_function[kernel_func](
        Q,
        K,
        V,
        O,
        grid_dim=(Int(Q.dim[1]()) // BD, Int(Q.dim[0]()) // BN),
        block_dim=(32),
    )
